Let Phi be a stationary simple locally finite planar point process with finite positive intensity, bounded Voronoi cells, finite nonempty edge-neighbor sets, no four cocircular points, no three collinear points, and almost surely unique nearest nuclei p_x at deterministic observation points. This is a conditional correlation-transfer result and does not construct a Riesz Gibbs phase.

from_statement: DRAFT; independent review pending. A measure-preserving map T is dynamically mixing when mu(T^(-n)A intersect B) tends to mu(A)mu(B) for each fixed event pair. That condition supplies no rate, no growing-window size control, no planar Delaunay stabilization, and no empty-disk estimate. It cannot by itself be used as the quantitative point-process alpha hypothesis of a Delaunay covariance bridge. A Bernoulli shift illustrates the quantifier distinction: for an event B of probability 1/2 and A_n=T^nB, the unrestricted event covariance equals 1/4 for every n despite fixed-event mixing. This does not deny independence of separated finite Bernoulli windows.
to_statement: Let (X,Sigma,mu) be a probability space and T: X -> X measure-preserving. T is (strongly) mixing if mu(T^{-n}A cap B) -> mu(A)mu(B) as n -> infinity for all measurable A, B in Sigma, so that the sets T^{-n}A become asymptotically independent of B in the measure-theoretic sense. Strong mixing implies weak mixing (the Cesaro-averaged statement (1/N) sum_{n=0}^{N-1} |mu(T^{-n}A cap B) - mu(A)mu(B)| -> 0), and weak mixing implies ergodicity; neither implication reverses in general.
